title: Florida House, District 107
what_it_does: Represents District 107 (Part of Miami-Dade) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: Wallace Aristide (Democratic) is listed as unopposed by the Florida Division of Elections and is elected without appearing on the November ballot. Source: https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp

candidates.name: Wallace Aristide
candidates.occupation: Educator; former principal of Miami Northwestern Senior High School
candidates.background: Wallace Aristide of Miami was born in Nassau, Bahamas, moved to Florida in 1969 and spent about 35 years in Miami-Dade public schools, including as principal of Miami Northwestern Senior High; he was named Principal of the Year in 2014. He holds a criminal-justice degree from Bethune-Cookman University and a master's in education from Nova Southeastern. He ran for the Miami-Dade County Commission in 2022 and was elected to the Florida House in 2024.

immigration.summary: Voted against SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.

elections.summary: Voted no on CS/CS/HB 991 when it passed the House on Feb. 25, 2026 and no on final House passage March 12, 2026. CS/CS/HB 991 (2026), now law (Ch. 2026-26), requires the state to verify voters' U.S. citizenship using driver-license and other government records and removes student and retirement-home IDs from the IDs accepted at the polls.

record.item: Voted against SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.

Voted no on CS/HB 1517 (2025), which would have allowed parents to sue for the wrongful death of an unborn child (excluding the mother and providers of lawful care); passed the House 79-32 on April 9, 2025 and died in the Senate.

Voted no on CS/HB 289 (2026), which would have allowed parents to sue for the wrongful death of an unborn child (excluding the mother and providers of lawful care); passed the House 76-34 on Jan. 15, 2026 and died in the Senate.

Voted no on final House passage of CS/HB 1205 (2025), the law (Ch. 2025-21) that added new rules, registration requirements and penalties for citizen initiative petition drives; passed 81-30 on May 1, 2025.
